summary: Project c33d0000-e29b-41d4-a716-446655440003 passed the declared clean-tree check: `git diff --exit-code HEAD --` exited 0 with no output. Source inspection shows an adapter-free Rust library and CLI that accepts ToolMetadata plus InvocationEnvelope and emits deterministic allow, deny, or review_required receipts (`README.md:5-13`, `src/policy.rs:23-158`), with documented CLI exit codes 0/2/3 and input/internal error codes 64/65/70 (`README.md:89-107`, `src/receipt.rs:30-37`, `src/main.rs:35-70`). Integration risks are that execution, authentication, authorization, storage, and sandboxing are explicitly external responsibilities (`README.md:156-158`); target authorization supports only exact, global `*`, or trailing-prefix wildcard matching (`src/policy.rs:160-168`); and the published input schemas accept unconstrained strings and unspecified extra properties, including no date-time format enforcement for requested_at_utc (`schemas/invocation-envelope.schema.json:5-14`). Existing integration tests cover allowed read-only operation, missing-trace denial, critical review routing, receipt schema/version, and CLI deny exit code (`tests/policy_decisions.rs:34-64`, `tests/cli_contract.rs:4-35`). Recommended next operator action: define the runtime adapter that maps catalog metadata and invocation targets into these schemas, enforce deny/review receipts before execution, and explicitly harden or accept the current target-pattern and schema-validation semantics before integration.
